reasoning_traces.think:
The MetricHonesty primitive formalizes the notion of calibration as a statistical property of a prediction pool rather than an individual forecast. It is defined by how often predicted confidence levels align with actual outcomes across all settled picks. This is mathematically expressed through a reliability diagram or Brier score decomposition. The dual nature lies between probabilistic forecasting and empirical validation—wherein a model's internal confidence distribution must reflect true outcome frequencies. Failure modes include overconfidence or underconfidence in small samples, especially when fewer than 100 picks exist, leading to unreliable estimates. The metric does not guarantee correctness of any single prediction but evaluates long-run consistency. In GSI, this supports Bayesian inference by validating prior-to-posterior alignment. In GSE, it enables adaptive reasoning systems that adjust belief states based on calibration feedback.
